# dist/esm apps resolve basePath to the repo root, so the built tree never runs

## Context

Reported by @tobiu, 2026-08-31: opening `http://localhost:63342/neo/dist/esm/apps/portal/index.html#/home` renders the portal home **fully** — including offscreen canvases — while the app worker emits the same rejection thousands of times.

```
Base.mjs:411  Uncaught (in promise) undefined
(anonymous)         @ Base.mjs:411
promiseMessage      @ Base.mjs:405
(anonymous)         @ RemoteMethodAccess.mjs:164
(anonymous)         @ Body.mjs:1271
Promise.then
onStoreLoad         @ Body.mjs:1270
fire                @ Observable.mjs:284
onCollectionMutate  @ Store.mjs:1082
fire                @ Observable.mjs:284
splice              @ Base.mjs:1608
appendFeedBatch     @ Workspace.mjs:620
(anonymous)         @ Workspace.mjs:567
```

The rendering is genuinely correct. The defect this ticket files is what that trace proves about **which tree is executing**.

## The Problem — measured

**1. The built artifacts exist and are minified.**

| file | newlines |
|---|---:|
| `dist/esm/src/worker/Base.mjs` | **0** (4850 bytes, single line) |
| `dist/esm/apps/portal/app.mjs` | **0** |
| `apps/portal/app.mjs` (source) | 7 |

**2. There are no source maps.** `find dist/esm -name '*.map'` → **0 files**; `grep sourceMappingURL dist/esm/src/worker/Base.mjs` → **0**.

**3. Therefore the reported line numbers cannot come from the built tree.** A stack against a single-line file can only ever read `Base.mjs:1`. `Base.mjs:411`, `Body.mjs:1271`, `Workspace.mjs:620` are **source** line numbers — and `src/worker/Base.mjs:405` is `return new Promise(function(resolve, reject) {`, exactly the `promiseMessage` frame the trace names.

**4. The emitted config points away from the emitted tree.** `dist/esm/apps/portal/neo-config.json`:

```json
{"appPath": "apps/portal/app.mjs", "basePath": "../../../../", "workerBasePath": "../../src/worker/"}
```

Resolved from `dist/esm/apps/portal/` on disk:

| value | resolves to |
|---|---|
| `basePath: "../../../../"` | `<repo>` — **the repository root** |
| `workerBasePath: "../../src/worker/"` | `<repo>/dist/esm/src/worker/` |

The source config carries `basePath: "../../"`, which from `apps/portal/` is also the repository root. `esmDistTransforms#rewriteNeoConfig` prefixes `../../` because the config moves two directories deeper — arithmetic that **preserves the original destination**. Its JSDoc states that intent: *"basePath gains `../../` because the config moves two directories deeper in the output tree … it compensates for where the config now sits."* Preserving the destination is the defect: a built app must resolve against the tree holding its own copied engine, so the value should remain `../../`, which from the new location means `dist/esm`.

**So `dist/esm/apps/portal/index.html` does not exercise the `dist/esm` build.** It is a correct, complete, emitted tree that the runtime is configured to walk past. That is why it "fully works": the source tree works. Every defect the emitted tree could carry is invisible through this entry point.

## What is NOT established

Stated explicitly so the next reader does not inherit a guess:

- **The rejection's root cause.** `worker/Base.mjs:311` rejects with `promise.reject(data.data)`, so an `undefined` reason means a reply arrived with `reject` set and no payload. Which remote call refuses, and why, is **not** diagnosed here. `Neo.main.DomAccess.scrollTo` itself cannot throw — it is `this.getElement(id)?.scrollTo(...)`, a no-op on a missing node.
- **The exact resolution path** by which `appPath` becomes a URL. The `basePath` arithmetic above is measured on disk; the runtime's consumption of it was not traced to a single line.
- Whether the same re-anchoring affects `dist/production` / `dist/development`.

## The Fix

1. `rewriteNeoConfig` must re-anchor `basePath` to the emitted tree rather than preserve its original destination — the built value should resolve to `dist/esm`, not to the repository root. `isFixedBasePath` (absolute / protocol-relative) keeps its existing pass-through.
2. A regression arm that asserts the **resolved** target, not the string: from `dist/esm/apps/<app>/`, `basePath` must resolve inside `dist/esm`. A string comparison would have passed every version of this bug.
3. The amplifier is separable and worth its own line: `grid/Body.mjs:1270` dispatches `Neo.main.DomAccess.scrollTo` as `.then()` with **no `.catch()`**, so any refusal becomes an unhandled rejection; `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:566` runs a `setInterval` feed that mutates the store every tick, re-entering `onStoreLoad`. One refusal per tick is what turns a single fault into thousands of console lines. Fixing the resolution may silence this instance without fixing the pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `dist/esm/apps/<app>/neo-config.json`'s `basePath` resolves inside `dist/esm`, asserted by resolution rather than string equality.
- [ ] A built portal loaded from `dist/esm/apps/portal/index.html` executes the **built** modules — provable because a deliberate edit to a `dist/esm/src/**` file changes observed behaviour, and the equivalent source edit does not.
- [ ] `isFixedBasePath` values (absolute, protocol-relative, fully-qualified) still pass through unchanged, with an arm each.
- [ ] The remote-call refusal behind the reported trace is either fixed or filed with its own root cause; this ticket does not claim to have diagnosed it.

## Out of Scope

- The `.then()`-without-`.catch()` pattern at `grid/Body.mjs:1270` and the workstation feed interval — the amplifier, not the fault.
- `#17972`'s `WS/` addon dynamic import: same class (runtime reaching unbuilt source) via a different mechanism — a dynamic import inside `Main.mjs` rather than a static config value, and in a consumer workspace rather than the in-repo portal.
- Typing the reply-path rejection at `worker/Base.mjs:311`. `#17894` typed the dead-port path today; this one still rejects with whatever the reply carries.

## Related

- `#17931` — the `dist/esm` boot arm. This is the defect that arm exists to catch, and could not be seen by a resolution-only fixture: every path it checks genuinely exists.
- `#17972` — sibling in the same class, different mechanism.
- `#17921` — the three original `dist/esm` load defects; this is a fourth on the same surface.

## Premise falsified — my own ticket. `basePath` is not in the boot chain, and the prescribed fix is a regression

I claimed this lane to implement Fix item 1. Before the first edit I traced the one thing this ticket's own **"What is NOT established"** section admits it never traced:

> *"The exact resolution path by which `appPath` becomes a URL. The `basePath` arithmetic above is measured on disk; the runtime's consumption of it was not traced to a single line."*

Traced now, and it refutes the ticket. **`dist/esm/apps/portal/index.html` does execute the `dist/esm` build**, and `basePath` plays no part in getting there.

### The boot chain, hop by hop — every hop lands inside `dist/esm`

| # | resolver | value | resolves against | lands on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `index.html` `<script type="module" src>` | `../../src/MicroLoader.mjs` | the document URL `dist/esm/apps/portal/` | `dist/esm/src/MicroLoader.mjs` |
| 2 | `MicroLoader.mjs:1` — `new URL('./neo-config.json', document.baseURI)` | `./neo-config.json` | `document.baseURI` | `dist/esm/apps/portal/neo-config.json` |
| 3 | `MicroLoader.mjs:3` — `import(d.mainPath)` | `mainPath: './Main.mjs'` | **the importing module's URL**, `dist/esm/src/` | `dist/esm/src/Main.mjs` |
| 4 | `worker/Manager.mjs:239` — `(opts.basePath \|\| Neo.config.workerBasePath) + fileName`, then `new Worker(url)` | `workerBasePath: '../../src/worker/'` | the document URL (Worker URLs resolve against the document) | `dist/esm/src/worker/` |
| 5 | `worker/App.mjs:378` — ``importApp(path) → import(`../../${path}.mjs`)`` | `appPath: 'apps/portal/app.mjs'` | **`App.mjs`'s own module URL**, `dist/esm/src/worker/` | `dist/esm/apps/portal/app.mjs` |

Every one of those files exists in the emitted tree and every one is minified — `MicroLoader.mjs`, `Main.mjs`, `worker/App.mjs`, `apps/portal/app.mjs`, `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs`, `src/grid/Body.mjs`: **0 newlines each**.

`appPath` is never joined to `basePath`. It is a *module-relative* specifier consumed inside the worker, and hop 5 is the load-bearing one: `../../` from `dist/esm/src/worker/` is `dist/esm/`, so it addresses the built app. Same shape at `worker/Canvas.mjs:118`, `worker/Task.mjs:52` and `worker/Data.mjs:92`. **`basePath` appears nowhere in the chain.**

### What `basePath` is actually for, and why the repository root is correct

`dist/esm` is not a self-contained tree. `ls dist/esm` → `ServiceWorker.mjs apps dist docs examples src`. Three resolvers depend on `basePath` reaching *past* it:

| consumer | expression | needs |
|---|---|---|
| `DefaultConfig.mjs:379` | `resourcesPath = basePath + 'resources/'` | the repository-root `resources/` — `dist/esm/resources` does not exist |
| `Stylesheet.mjs:53` (the `dist/esm` branch) | `basePath + 'node_modules/@fortawesome/fontawesome-free/css/all.min.css'` | the repository-root `node_modules/` — never copied into `dist/esm` |
| `Stylesheet.mjs:78` and `:105` | `rootPath = config.basePath.substring(6)`, then `` `${rootPath}css/${folder}/…` `` | **strip exactly `../../`** off the emitted value to land on the *dist-mode root*, `dist/esm/css/…` — written by `buildScripts/build/themes.mjs:236` under `themes.mjs -e esm` |

That `substring(6)` is the decisive witness. It is only correct if the emitted `basePath` is two levels *above* the dist-mode root — which is precisely the `../../../../` this ticket calls a defect.

### And it is a convention, not an accident

```
dist/esm/apps/portal/neo-config.json         basePath "../../../../"   workerBasePath "../../src/worker/"
dist/production/apps/portal/neo-config.json  basePath "../../../../"   workerBasePath "../../"
```

Both dist modes anchor `basePath` at the repository root and `workerBasePath` at the dist-mode root. The two anchors differ **on purpose**: one addresses emitted modules, the other addresses assets that were never emitted.

And the value is not unowned. @neo-opus-vega's #17918 — *"Dist CSS and Font Awesome roots die on absolute mounts — `substring(6)` is relative-only"* — is open and assigned against these same three consumers, and its body records that its implementation is **gated** on `D#17886`'s path contract and on #17884, which it states is `[PROVISIONAL_UNGRADUATED]`. So `basePath`'s dist semantics are a contested, pre-quorum surface with a named owner. Re-anchoring it out of this ticket would have mutated that contract from the side, before graduation, and under a premise that turns out to be false.

### What the prescribed fix would have shipped

Fix item 1 — *"the built value should resolve to `dist/esm`, not to the repository root"* — emits `basePath: "../../"`. That:

1. sends `resourcesPath` to `dist/esm/resources/` — **absent**;
2. sends the `dist/esm` fontawesome href to `dist/esm/node_modules/…` — **absent**;
3. turns `basePath.substring(6)` into `''`, requesting theme CSS from `dist/esm/apps/portal/css/…` instead of `dist/esm/css/…` — **every theme stylesheet 404s**;
4. diverges `dist/esm` from `dist/production` on a value they deliberately share.

None of it changes which app module executes, because hops 1–5 never read `basePath`. It is a pure regression, and the AC that was meant to catch regressions — *"`basePath` resolves inside `dist/esm`, asserted by resolution rather than string equality"* — would have **certified** it. An AC derived from a false premise is not a safety net; it is the premise wearing a test's clothes.

### Where the ticket's evidence actually points

The measurement that produced this ticket is sound and I am not retracting it: minified single-line files carry no source maps, so `Base.mjs:411` / `Body.mjs:1271` / `Workspace.mjs:620` cannot have been read off the `dist/esm` tree. What I got wrong is the inference. `basePath` is not a mechanism that could redirect module execution, so it cannot be the explanation — and I have not established what is. Notably the trace names `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` while the reported URL is the **portal**, which the ticket never reconciled. Whichever context produced those frames is still open, and it is not this one.

**The part of @tobiu's report that survives intact is the storm itself**, which this ticket pushed out of scope as *"the amplifier, not the fault"*. With the fault falsified, the amplifier is the whole finding, and it is real at source regardless of which tree runs:

- `src/grid/Body.mjs:1269-1277` — `me.timeout(50).then(() => { Neo.main.DomAccess.scrollTo({…}) })`, **no `.catch()`**.
- `src/worker/Base.mjs:311` — the reply path calls `promise.reject(data.data)`; #17894 typed the dead-port *reason* but nothing added a *handler*.
- `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` — `appendFeedBatch` mutates the store on a ticking feed, re-entering `onStoreLoad` and re-dispatching the unhandled call every tick. One refusal becomes thousands of console lines.

### Disposition

Closing this as **not planned — premise falsified**, rather than re-scoping in place: the title, Context, Problem, Fix and all four ACs are about `basePath`, and a body rewritten around a different mechanism is a body nobody can read against its own history. The surviving symptom gets its own ticket with its own root cause, which is what this ticket said it would not claim to have.

Successor: **#18010** — *A fire-and-forget remote dispatch turns an expected teardown reject into an unhandled-rejection storm*. It carries the three sites above, a census of the wider surface (97 `Neo.main.*` dispatch sites in `src/**`, 8 of them inside a `.then()` with no `.catch()`), and it routes the engine-wide disposition to a Discussion rather than settling it in a bug ticket.

No code was changed on this lane. The `esmDistTransforms` / `esmWorkspaceBuild` arms I had scoped are withdrawn with it — the existing `'a relative basePath still gains the output-tree offset'` arm in `esmDistTransforms.spec.mjs` is **correct as written** and stays.

🖖 Grace
